Supplementary Information

These Supplementary Notes give complete proofs of the results stated in the main text. Supplementary Note 1 collects the Walsh–Fourier facts that underlie the spectral analysis. Supplementary Note 2 proves the generalization bounds, Supplementary Note 3 proves the results on capped error reduction, and Supplementary Note 4 proves the results on budget-aware noise control. Each result is restated with its number from the main text before its proof.

Supplementary Note 1. Walsh–Fourier coordinates

The coordinates in which quantum noise acts most simply are the characters of ℤ2n\mathbb{Z}_{2}^{n}. For A⊆[n]A\subseteq[n] define the Walsh character and, for a distribution qq and a function ϕ\phi on 𝒳\mathcal{X}, the associated coefficients

χA​(x):=(−1)∑i∈Axi,q^​(A):=𝔼x∼q​[χA​(x)],ϕ^​(A):=2−n​∑t∈𝒳ϕ⁡(t)​χA​(t).\displaystyle\chi_{A}(x):=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in A}x_{i}},\qquad\widehat{q}(A):=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim q}\bigl[\chi_{A}(x)\bigr],\qquad\widehat{\phi}(A):=2^{-n}\sum_{t\in\mathcal{X}}\phi(t)\chi_{A}(t). (S1)

Characters are multiplicative, χA​(x⊕y)=χA​(x)​χA​(y)\chi_{A}(x\oplus y)=\chi_{A}(x)\chi_{A}(y), and orthonormal under the uniform measure. Three facts will be used.

(i) Coefficients are Pauli observables.

Since ZA​|x⟩=χA​(x)​|x⟩Z_{A}\ket{x}=\chi_{A}(x)\ket{x} for ZA:=⨂i∈AZiZ_{A}:=\bigotimes_{i\in A}Z_{i},

qθ𝒩^​(A)=Tr⁡[ρθ𝒩​ZA].\displaystyle\widehat{q_{\theta}^{\mathcal{N}}}(A)=\Tr\bigl[\rho_{\theta}^{\mathcal{N}}Z_{A}\bigr]. (S2)

The Walsh coefficients of the output distribution are exactly the computational-basis Pauli correlators of the output state, so |A||A| is the order of the correlation described by the mode.

(ii) Parseval links the spectrum to the collision probability.

Writing coll⁡(q):=∑xq​(x)2\mathrm{coll}(q):=\sum_{x}q(x)^{2} for the probability that two independent draws from qq agree,

∑A⊆[n]q^​(A)2=2n​coll​(q),∑A⊆[n]ϕ^​(A)2=𝔼x,y∼u​[ϕ​(x⊕y)2].\displaystyle\sum_{A\subseteq[n]}\widehat{q}(A)^{2}=2^{n}\,\mathrm{coll}(q),\qquad\sum_{A\subseteq[n]}\widehat{\phi}(A)^{2}=\mathbb{E}_{x,y\sim u}\bigl[\phi(x\oplus y)^{2}\bigr]. (S3)

The uniform distribution attains coll⁡(u)=2−n\mathrm{coll}(u)=2^{-n}, so 2n​coll​(q)2^{n}\mathrm{coll}(q) measures how far qq is from flat and, by equation (S3), simultaneously budgets the total spectral mass available to the generator. This is the quantity through which the ansatz enters our complexity bound.

(iii) Translation-invariant kernels are diagonal.

We call κ\kappa translation invariant if

κ⁡(x,y)=ϕ⁡(x⊕y)for some ​ϕ:𝒳→ℝ,ϕ⁡(𝟎)=1,\displaystyle\kappa(x,y)=\phi(x\oplus y)\qquad\text{for some }\phi:\mathcal{X}\to\mathbb{R},\quad\phi(\mathbf{0})=1, (S4)

the normalization being without loss of generality. The Gram matrix GG with entries Gx​y=κ⁡(x,y)G_{xy}=\kappa(x,y) is then diagonalized by the characters, with G​χA=2n​ϕ^​(A)​χAG\chi_{A}=2^{n}\widehat{\phi}(A)\chi_{A}, so κ\kappa is positive semidefinite if and only if ϕ^​(A)≥0\widehat{\phi}(A)\geq 0 for all AA, and in that case ∑Aϕ^​(A)=ϕ⁡(𝟎)=1\sum_{A}\widehat{\phi}(A)=\phi(\mathbf{0})=1. The Gaussian kernel on the Hamming distance used in the main text, κ(x,y)=1c∑i=1cexp[−dH(x,y)/(2τi2)]\kappa(x,y)=\frac{1}{c}\sum_{i=1}^{c}\exp[-d_{H}(x,y)/(2\tau_{i}^{2})], is of this form with ϕ⁡(t)=1c​∑i=1cai|t|\phi(t)=\frac{1}{c}\sum_{i=1}^{c}a_{i}^{|t|} and ai=e−1/(2τi2)a_{i}=e^{-1/(2\tau_{i}^{2})}.

Under equation (S4), multiplicativity of the characters gives the witness its spectral form,

hθ𝒩​(x)=∑A⊆[n]ϕ^​(A)​qθ𝒩^​(A)​χA​(x),\displaystyle h_{\theta}^{\mathcal{N}}(x)=\sum_{A\subseteq[n]}\widehat{\phi}(A)\,\widehat{q_{\theta}^{\mathcal{N}}}(A)\,\chi_{A}(x), (S5)

so the witness is a kernel-weighted superposition of the generator’s Pauli correlators. In particular the uniform distribution has u^​(A)=0\widehat{u}(A)=0 for A≠∅A\neq\varnothing, so its witness hu≡ϕ^​(∅)h_{u}\equiv\widehat{\phi}(\varnothing) is constant. By equation (10), the class may therefore be recentered at no cost,

(Pm−P)​hθ𝒩=(Pm−P)​h¯θ𝒩,h¯θ𝒩:=hθ𝒩−hu=∑A≠∅ϕ^​(A)​qθ𝒩^​(A)​χA.\displaystyle(P_{m}-P)h_{\theta}^{\mathcal{N}}=(P_{m}-P)\bar{h}_{\theta}^{\mathcal{N}},\qquad\bar{h}_{\theta}^{\mathcal{N}}:=h_{\theta}^{\mathcal{N}}-h_{u}=\sum_{A\neq\varnothing}\widehat{\phi}(A)\widehat{q_{\theta}^{\mathcal{N}}}(A)\chi_{A}. (S6)

We write ℋ¯𝒩\bar{\mathcal{H}}^{\mathcal{N}} and ℋ¯±𝒩\bar{\mathcal{H}}_{\pm}^{\mathcal{N}} for the corresponding centered and symmetrized classes, and h¯θ:=h¯θ0\bar{h}_{\theta}:=\bar{h}^{0}_{\theta} in the noiseless case.

Supplementary Note 2. Proofs of the generalization bounds

We first prove the reduction to the learned witness, which underlies both generalization theorems, and then the noise-agnostic bound, the noiseless complexity bound, and the bounds under scrambled local Pauli noise.

See 1

Proof of Lemma 1.

For brevity, we condition on 𝒮\mathcal{S} and θ^𝒩\hat{\theta}_{\mathcal{N}} and write

q:=qθ^𝒩𝒩,h:=hθ^𝒩𝒩.\displaystyle q:=q_{\hat{\theta}_{\mathcal{N}}}^{\mathcal{N}},\qquad h:=h_{\hat{\theta}_{\mathcal{N}}}^{\mathcal{N}}. (S7)

Under this conditioning, the learned distribution qq and the witness hh are fixed, while

𝒴=(y1,…,yN)∼q⊗N.\displaystyle\mathcal{Y}=(y_{1},\ldots,y_{N})\sim q^{\otimes N}. (S8)

We set the population target-only and generator-only terms by

Ap\displaystyle A_{p} :=𝔼x,x′∼p​[κ⁡(x,x′)],\displaystyle:=\mathbb{E}_{x,x^{\prime}\sim p}\left[\kappa(x,x^{\prime})\right], Aq\displaystyle A_{q} :=𝔼y,y′∼q​[κ⁡(y,y′)].\displaystyle:=\mathbb{E}_{y,y^{\prime}\sim q}\left[\kappa(y,y^{\prime})\right]. (S9)

Since P​h=𝔼x∼p,y∼q​[κ⁡(x,y)]Ph=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim p,\,y\sim q}[\kappa(x,y)] by the definition of the witness, equation (8), the population risk can then be written as

R𝒩​(θ^𝒩)=Aq+Ap−2​P​h.\displaystyle R_{\mathcal{N}}(\hat{\theta}_{\mathcal{N}})=A_{q}+A_{p}-2Ph. (S10)

Similarly, we write the empirical risk as

Let

ηk​(P)\displaystyle\eta_{k}(P) =−δk​πk​(P)+𝒪⁡(ϵk​δk),P≠I.\displaystyle=-\delta_{k}\pi_{k}(P)+\mathcal{O}(\epsilon_{k}\delta_{k}),\qquad P\neq I. (S64)

which proves equation (43). Neglecting the accumulated higher-order term in the weak-noise regime and exponentiating yields equation (44). ∎

Proof of Lemma 4.

It is equivalent to minimize ∑krk2\sum_{k}r_{k}^{2}. Suppose that two residual rates satisfy ri<rjr_{i}<r_{j} and ri<ϵir_{i}<\epsilon_{i}. Moving a sufficiently small amount δ>0\delta>0 from rjr_{j} to rir_{i} preserves the total residual noise and all feasibility constraints, while changing the objective by

(ri+δ)2+(rj−δ)2−ri2−rj2\displaystyle(r_{i}+\delta)^{2}+(r_{j}-\delta)^{2}-r_{i}^{2}-r_{j}^{2}
=2​δ​(ri−rj)+2​δ2<0.\displaystyle\qquad=2\delta(r_{i}-r_{j})+2\delta^{2}<0. (S68)

Thus, all residual rates not limited by their physical upper bounds must be equal. Locations whose physical rates are below this common level remain unchanged. Hence,

rkcap​(R)=min⁡{ϵk,ν⁡(R)}.\displaystyle r_{k}^{\mathrm{cap}}(R)=\min\{\epsilon_{k},\nu(R)\}. (S69)

The budget constraint determines ν⁡(R)\nu(R), and uniqueness follows from the strict convexity of ∑krk2\sum_{k}r_{k}^{2}. ∎

This note proves the sensitivity of the risk to parameter changes, the cumulative regret bound and its rate.

We first bound the validation-error contribution to RegT\operatorname{Reg}_{T},

Together with equation (S91), the probe and radius contributions are at most (15+6​z)​Γ¯2​T​J​H​log⁡(8​J​H/β)/(α​B)(15+6z)\,\overline{\Gamma}^{2}\,T\sqrt{JH\log(8JH/\beta)/(\alpha B)}.

Changes between comparisons.

It remains to bound the score-change contribution in equation (S73),

∑s∈ℐ∑t=ss+ws−1[Ψt​(js)−Ψs​(js)+Ψs​(js⋆)−minj⁡Ψt​(j)].\displaystyle\sum_{s\in\mathcal{I}}\sum_{t=s}^{s+w_{s}-1}\left[\Psi_{t}(j_{s})-\Psi_{s}(j_{s})+\Psi_{s}(j_{s}^{\star})-\min_{j}\Psi_{t}(j)\right]. (S95)

This term tracks changes in both the retained candidate’s score and the best available score. The minimum score changes by at most the largest change among individual candidate scores. Hence, within a block,

Ψt​(js)−Ψs​(js)+Ψs​(js⋆)−minj⁡Ψt​(j)\displaystyle\Psi_{t}(j_{s})-\Psi_{s}(j_{s})+\Psi_{s}(j_{s}^{\star})-\min_{j}\Psi_{t}(j)
=Ψt​(js)−Ψs​(js)+minj⁡Ψs​(j)−minj⁡Ψt​(j)\displaystyle\quad=\Psi_{t}(j_{s})-\Psi_{s}(j_{s})+\min_{j}\Psi_{s}(j)-\min_{j}\Psi_{t}(j)
≤|Ψt​(js)−Ψs​(js)|+|minj⁡Ψs​(j)−minj⁡Ψt​(j)|\displaystyle\quad\leq|\Psi_{t}(j_{s})-\Psi_{s}(j_{s})|+\left|\min_{j}\Psi_{s}(j)-\min_{j}\Psi_{t}(j)\right|
≤2∑τ=st−1maxj|Ψτ+1(j)−Ψτ(j)|(telescoping).\displaystyle\quad\leq 2\sum_{\tau=s}^{t-1}\max_{j}|\Psi_{\tau+1}(j)-\Psi_{\tau}(j)|\qquad\text{(telescoping)}. (S96)

Summing over blocks gives

∑s∈ℐ∑t=ss+ws−1[Ψt​(js)−Ψs​(js)+Ψs​(js⋆)−minj⁡Ψt​(j)]\displaystyle\sum_{s\in\mathcal{I}}\sum_{t=s}^{s+w_{s}-1}\left[\Psi_{t}(j_{s})-\Psi_{s}(j_{s})+\Psi_{s}(j_{s}^{\star})-\min_{j}\Psi_{t}(j)\right]
≤2​∑s∈ℐ∑τ=ss+ws−2(s+ws−1−τ)​maxj​|Ψτ+1​(j)−Ψτ​(j)|\displaystyle\quad\leq 2\sum_{s\in\mathcal{I}}\sum_{\tau=s}^{s+w_{s}-2}(s+w_{s}-1-\tau)\max_{j}|\Psi_{\tau+1}(j)-\Psi_{\tau}(j)|
≤2​(K−1)​∑t=0T−2maxj⁡|Ψt+1​(j)−Ψt​(j)|.\displaystyle\quad\leq 2(K-1)\sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\max_{j}|\Psi_{t+1}(j)-\Psi_{t}(j)|. (S97)

The first inequality interchanges the finite sums. The second uses ws≤Kw_{s}\leq K and the disjoint block interiors, and empty sums are zero.

We bound the remaining score variation through parameter movement and changes in the affordable shot allowance. By Lemma 5 and Assumption 3,

∑t=0T−2maxj⁡|Ψt+1​(j)−Ψt​(j)|\displaystyle\sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\max_{j}|\Psi_{t+1}(j)-\Psi_{t}(j)|
≤LR​∑t=0T−2‖θt+1−θt‖2+λ​Γ¯2​∑t=0T−2|Nfuture,t+1−1−Nfuture,t−1|\displaystyle\quad\leq L_{R}\sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\|\theta_{t+1}-\theta_{t}\|_{2}+\lambda\overline{\Gamma}^{2}\sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\left|N_{\mathrm{future},t+1}^{-1}-N_{\mathrm{future},t}^{-1}\right|
≤LR​h​∑t=0T−21t+1+λ​Γ¯2​∑t=0T−2|Nfuture,t+1−1−Nfuture,t−1|.\displaystyle\quad\leq L_{R}h\sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\frac{1}{t+1}+\lambda\overline{\Gamma}^{2}\sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\left|N_{\mathrm{future},t+1}^{-1}-N_{\mathrm{future},t}^{-1}\right|. (S98)

The training allocation rule further implies

Nfuture,t+1\displaystyle N_{\mathrm{future},t+1} =(T−t)​Nfuture,t−⌊Nfuture,t⌋T−t−1\displaystyle=\frac{(T-t)N_{\mathrm{future},t}-\lfloor N_{\mathrm{future},t}\rfloor}{T-t-1}
=Nfuture,t+Nfuture,t−⌊Nfuture,t⌋T−t−1≥Nfuture,t.\displaystyle=N_{\mathrm{future},t}+\frac{N_{\mathrm{future},t}-\lfloor N_{\mathrm{future},t}\rfloor}{T-t-1}\geq N_{\mathrm{future},t}. (S99)

Thus,

∑t=0T−2|Nfuture,t+1−1−Nfuture,t−1|\displaystyle\sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\left|N_{\mathrm{future},t+1}^{-1}-N_{\mathrm{future},t}^{-1}\right| =1Nfuture,0−1Nfuture,T−1\displaystyle=\frac{1}{N_{\mathrm{future},0}}-\frac{1}{N_{\mathrm{future},T-1}} (monotonicity and telescoping)
≤1Nfuture,0.\displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{N_{\mathrm{future},0}}. (S100)

Together with ∑t=0T−2(t+1)−1≤1+log⁡T\sum_{t=0}^{T-2}(t+1)^{-1}\leq 1+\log T, this gives

Substitution into equation (S97) therefore bounds the cumulative score-change contribution by

2​(K−1)​[LR​h​(1+log⁡T)+λ​Γ¯2Nfuture,0].\displaystyle 2(K-1)\left[L_{R}h(1+\log T)+\frac{\lambda\overline{\Gamma}^{2}}{N_{\mathrm{future},0}}\right]. (S102)
Combining the bounds.

The validation and probe events hold jointly with probability at least 1−β1-\beta by a union bound. On this event, substituting the bounds on the validation, probe, radius and score-change into equation (S73) yields

RegT≤\displaystyle\operatorname{Reg}_{T}\leq{} (15+6​z)​Γ¯2​T​J​H​log⁡(8​J​H/β)α​B\displaystyle(15+6z)\overline{\Gamma}^{2}T\sqrt{\frac{JH\log(8JH/\beta)}{\alpha B}}
+2​av​(β)​(δγ​∑s∈ℐws​Ds+2​T​εtol)\displaystyle+2a_{v}(\beta)\left(\delta_{\gamma}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{I}}w_{s}D_{s}+2T\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}\right)
+2​(K−1)​[LR​h​(1+log⁡T)+λ​Γ¯2Nfuture,0],\displaystyle+2(K-1)\left[L_{R}h(1+\log T)+\frac{\lambda\overline{\Gamma}^{2}}{N_{\mathrm{future},0}}\right], (S103)

which proves the theorem. ∎

H=⌈TK⌉≤TK+1≤2​TK≤2​T1/3.\displaystyle H=\left\lceil\frac{T}{K}\right\rceil\leq\frac{T}{K}+1\leq\frac{2T}{K}\leq 2T^{1/3}. (S104)

For the validation term, κ∈[0,1]\kappa\in[0,1] implies

Thus ∑sws​Ds≤2​T\sum_{s}w_{s}D_{s}\leq\sqrt{2}\,T, and

2​av​(β)​(δγ​∑sws​Ds+2​T​εtol)\displaystyle 2a_{v}(\beta)\left(\delta_{\gamma}\sum_{s}w_{s}D_{s}+2T\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}\right)
≤2​T​av​(β)​(2​δγ+2​εtol)=𝒪⁡(T​log⁡(2/β)v).\displaystyle\qquad\leq 2Ta_{v}(\beta)\left(\sqrt{2}\,\delta_{\gamma}+2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}\right)=\mathcal{O}\!\left(T\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\beta)}{v}}\right). (S107)

which is independent of TT. Since K−1<T2/3K-1<T^{2/3}, the last term satisfies
